issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 6.2 asserts that for any eigenpair trajectory as in Proposition 6.1, the simplified indicator equals $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}^2 - r^2 \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}^2$. However, its proof in Appendix C.1 relies on formula (C.2), which explicitly requires the Bessel function argument $x = \kappa_p \rho$ to be real so that Bessel functions with real arguments are real-valued. If $\kappa_p \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$, Bessel functions with argument $\kappa_p \rho$ are complex-valued, so $|v_p|^2$ couples $\kappa_p$ and $\overline{\kappa_p}$ and formula (C.2) does not apply. In fact, by Lemma A.1, $I(p) = 0$ (hence $\overline{I}(p) = 0$) for every non-real eigenvalue, whereas $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}^2 - r^2 \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}^2$ does not vanish in general for non-real eigenpairs. Thus, the result is false unless restricted to real eigenvalue trajectories.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\kappa_p \in \mathbb{R}$ (or restrict to real eigenvalue trajectories) to the statement of Proposition 6.2.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 6.2 fails for non-real eigenvalue branches. Downstream applications in the paper specifically study real branches near bifurcations and remain valid once the statement is restricted to real trajectories.
issues.title: Proposition 6.2 omits the hypothesis that the eigenvalue trajectory is real
issues.why_classification: Adding the local condition $\kappa_p \in \mathbb{R}$ fully resolves the defect without any new lemmas, proof architecture, or loss of the paper's advertised results on real bifurcation detection.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An immediate consequence is that, by \cref{cor:bifurc_sufficient}, a real (piecewise-smooth) eigenvalue trajectory undergoes bifurcation if and only if $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The text states that the bifurcation condition $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)} = r \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$ is equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$. However, on the inner circle $\partial B_r$, the line element is $ds = r\,d\theta$, which implies $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}^2 = \int_0^{2\pi} |v_p(r,\theta)|^2 r\,d\theta = r a_m \pi \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}^2$, whereas on the outer unit circle $\partial B_1$, $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}^2 = a_m \pi \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}^2$. Therefore, $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)} = r \|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$ is equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = \sqrt{r} \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$, which contradicts the claimed equality $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$ because $0 < r < 1$ and non-trivial eigenfunctions cannot vanish identically on the boundary.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed equivalence with $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = \sqrt{r} \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.
issues.overall_effect: The prose characterization of bifurcation on the annulus in terms of the equality of the boundary $L^2$ norms is incorrect.
issues.title: False equivalence between L-infinity and L2 boundary norm ratios on the annulus
issues.why_classification: This is a local prose error concerning the scaling of the boundary line element $ds = r\,d\theta$. Correcting it to include the factor $\sqrt{r}$ requires no new arguments and leaves the surrounding analysis intact.
